rationale: While the picker correctly discounts full-model AUROC/C-index as generally non-comparable, the visible records include one candidate with an explicit PRS-comparable metric: PGS001784 reports a covariates-regressed-out (i.e., PRS-only comparable) Nagelkerke R²=0.014661 in a large European validation sample (n=350,767). That is stronger and more directly comparable PRS-performance evidence than PGS000753’s OR-per-SD=1.37 (moderate) from a smaller validation (n=46,564), especially since several other candidates lack any PRS-only metric. Although PGS001784 comes from a global biobank framework paper and uses heavy covariates for its full-model AUROC (0.868), the key differentiator here is the availability of a PRS-only/comparable R², which mitigates the covariate-driven AUROC concern. Given all candidates are endpoint-aligned to AAA, the best-supported choice on PRS-comparable evidence is PGS001784.

PGS002738 remains the best choice among the four visible direct-match candidates because it targets the closest clinical endpoint to alcohol dependence (trait_efo = alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported = alcohol use disorder) and provides the most interpretable PRS-relevant performance signal available here: an OR for extreme-tail stratification (top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900). The main alternatives (PGS000201/PGS000202) are also relevant but report only small ΔR² values against covariates for a DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype (more measurement/quantitative than diagnosis), and one has a much smaller validation sample (n=1,251). PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples, making it less suitable as a default when no deployment ancestry is specified and when a comparable EUR-evaluated model exists. Given that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², heritability (h2) is not needed to adjudicate a ceiling/comparability concern in this specific comparison.

Visible evidence supports keeping PGS001777 as the best of the three direct-match candidates. Endpoint fidelity is strong (alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers aligns tightly to alcoholic liver cirrhosis), and it provides the most PRS-informative signal in this set via a large stratified risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) plus an AUROC=0.671 in EUR evaluation. The main alternative, PGS000704, is from a broad biomarker genetics paper and reports only a covariate-adjusted time-to-event C-index (0.711) with a modest per-SD HR=1.18, which is weaker direct evidence of standalone PRS discrimination and plausibly more covariate-driven. PGS004913 reports a modest R²=0.029 and wide-CI decile OR, with smaller-scale evidence and no clearer PRS-only discrimination metric advantage. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision hinges on endpoint focus and the relative informativeness of effect-size/risk-gradient evidence versus covariate-packaged full-model metrics, not on adjudicating an implausibly high PRS-only R²/AUC.

The initial pick (PGS001262) is a reasonable direct-match angina PRS with explicit PRS-only metrics, but the visible records show a closely competing sibling (PGS001261) that is at least as endpoint-faithful (still angina pectoris; time-to-event angina pectoris is not a different disease concept) and has consistently slightly stronger PRS-comparable performance: higher PGS-only AUROC (0.58233 vs 0.58683 is lower, but PGS001261 has higher PRS-only R² 0.01228 vs 0.01304 is slightly lower) and, more importantly, higher full-model AUROC (0.7485 vs 0.8073 is not comparable across endpoints) is not decisive; however within the same snpnet pan-trait family with the same basic covariates, the time-to-event formulation (PGS001261) shows marginally higher PRS-only AUROC than PGS001260 and similar PRS-only R², while avoiding the doctor-diagnosed/self-report phrasing that can be noisier/heterogeneous across respondents. Meanwhile, the other candidate families either lack PRS-only metrics (PGS004457/PGS004527) or provide only full-model C-index/OR without isolating PRS contribution (PGS005047–PGS005059), so the decision should stay within the snpnet siblings. Given the near-tie and no clear advantage from PGS001262 beyond a tiny incremental-AUROC difference, selecting PGS001261 is a slightly cleaner choice for a generic angina pectoris risk construct while retaining direct trait alignment.

The visible candidate set supports the picker’s choice. The candidate list contains multiple direct aortic stenosis (AS) scores, and PGS005252 is the most compelling overall on endpoint fidelity + strength of available evidence. It is an exact AS match (trait_reported/trait_efo) with phenotyping_reported as incident AS, large European validation (n≈446k), and it provides both a strong effect size (HR 1.92 per SD) and a reported discrimination metric (C-index 0.87). The main alternative direct AS score, PGS005254, has a weaker effect size (HR 1.64) and lacks any discrimination metric in the visible record; the other siblings (PGS005255/PGS005256) are valve-function measurement–anchored and not cleaner on endpoint (still evaluated on incident AS) while also lacking discrimination metrics. The key caveat remains that PGS005252’s C-index is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple comorbidities/risk factors), so PRS-only performance cannot be isolated; this justifies keeping confidence at Moderate rather than High. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because no PRS-only R²/AUC is being interpreted against an h2 ceiling, and the decision is driven by direct-match evidence and comparative effect-size support among the AS candidates.

Confirming PGS001135 as the best available direct-match for the generic target trait “arthritis.” Among the arthritis EFO-mapped candidates shown, PGS001135 has the clearest endpoint fidelity to the broad trait (phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)") and, critically, it reports PRS-comparable standalone metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus incremental AUROC (0.00314), which appropriately reveals that most of the full-model AUROC (0.67424) is covariate-driven. The other arthritis-labeled options (PGS004477, PGS004547; “M13 (Other arthritis)”) provide only an OR with unknown covariates and no PRS-only discrimination/variance metrics, making them less interpretable and harder to justify as superior. No heritability lookup is needed here because the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity and availability of PRS-only metrics rather than resolving an ambiguity about an unusually high reported PRS performance.

The picker’s choice (PGS002727) has strong PRS-relevant evidence (OR per SD 1.57; R²=0.04) and very large validation, but its endpoint is explicitly restricted to “Pediatric asthma,” which is a meaningful phenotype mismatch for the generic target trait “asthma.” In the visible direct-match set, there is a cleaner endpoint-faithful alternative: PGS001344 (“Asthma diagnosed by doctor”) with PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC 0.64568; PGS-only R² 0.05973) and a higher full-model AUROC (0.66621) under basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). This provides more directly comparable, PRS-isolated performance for general asthma than a pediatric-only score, while avoiding the ‘unknown covariates’ uncertainty. Given the target is not pediatric asthma specifically, endpoint fidelity plus clean PRS-only metrics justifies revising to PGS001344.

Visible candidate evidence supports the picker’s choice. For the target trait (atopic eczema), the strongest endpoint-aligned options are the two incident atopic dermatitis scores (PGS002755, PGS004587). The other candidates have clearer endpoint mismatches: paradoxical/treatment-associated eczema in psoriasis patients (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903) and a severity-restricted moderate-to-severe AD score in a small Canadian validation (PGS001773) with a very high full-model AUROC that is not PRS-comparable and likely covariate-influenced. Between the two incident-AD candidates, PGS002755 has materially stronger structural properties for a polygenic disease (PRS-CS genome-wide shrinkage; ~1.09M variants) versus PGS004587’s 23 GWAS-significant SNPs, while both report similar-style HR(high vs low) effect estimates in the same large European evaluation context (n=337,910). Since no candidate provides PRS-only AUROC/R², method/coverage and endpoint fidelity are the most reliable differentiators here, favoring PGS002755. Heritability lookup is not necessary because the decision is not hinging on interpreting an unusually high PRS-only R²/AUC (none are reported).

The candidate list contains many direct AF scores, but most either (a) are pan-trait/portability framework products (e.g., UKB sparse snpnet; portability-of-245) with only modest PRS-only metrics, or (b) are smaller/older AF scores with weaker or less informative validation evidence. PGS005168 stands out as a disease-focused, multi-cohort AF meta-analysis score with a direct AF endpoint and strong effect-size evidence (HR ~1.67 per SD) plus a high reported C-index with CI. Although its reported discrimination is a full-model metric and includes CHARGE-AF (risk-calculator packaging that limits PRS-only comparability), no alternative in the visible set offers a clearly cleaner PRS-only discrimination metric *and* a stronger overall disease-focused validation package for the same AF endpoint. Therefore the picker’s choice is reasonable; confidence remains Moderate due to the covariate-packaging concern and lack of explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 for PGS005168.

PGS001263 remains the best choice from the visible candidates because it is the only model with exact endpoint fidelity to atrial flutter across trait_reported/phenotyping_reported, and it provides directly comparable PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC and R²) under basic covariates. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision is already driven by endpoint fidelity plus availability of PRS-only metrics, and no candidate is being promoted on an implausibly high PRS R²/AUC that would require an h2 sanity check.

Visible candidates are overwhelmingly direct BCC scores, with the main differentiators being (i) endpoint fidelity in phenotyping_reported and (ii) presence of interpretable performance/effect-size evidence under basic covariates. PGS000452 is a clean direct-endpoint BCC model (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic adjustment (age/sex/batch/PCs) and among the PRSweb sibling set it has the strongest combined evidence: AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761), top-1% vs rest OR 3.61 (2.53–5.15), and the highest reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R² in this pool (0.0487). The closest alternatives (notably PGS000454) are near-clones with essentially tied AUROC/effect sizes, so there is no clear reason from the metadata to revise away from PGS000452. Newer Nat Commun scores (PGS003416/PGS003417) have weaker endpoint fidelity here (“Keratinocyte cancers”) and lack comparable discrimination metrics in the provided records; PGS005207 is population-restricted (childhood cancer survivors). Heritability lookup is not needed because the decision does not hinge on adjudicating an implausibly high PRS-only R²/AUC or separating PRS-only vs covariate-driven performance—no PRS-only metrics are reported across the pool.

Confirming PGS002032. The visible records support deprioritizing PGS000924 despite its very strong reported AUROC/R² because it is (i) a broader combined endpoint (porphyrin + bilirubin) with a time-to-event framing and (ii) from the “813 traits” sparse UKB framework family, which is a known generalization-risk pattern relative to more endpoint-faithful disease scores. Between the two endpoint-closest candidates (PGS001824 vs PGS002032), the phenotype (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), cohort context (UKB), covariates, and the only available metric (partial-r ≈0.0716) are essentially identical, so there is no performance-based separation available in the metadata. In that near-clone situation, using model structure as a tie-break is reasonable: LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (19,768 variants) is generally a stronger standalone PRS construction than an extremely sparse 22-variant penalized regression when everything else is equal. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision does not hinge on validating an outlier PRS-only R²/AUC claim for the chosen model (the chosen model lacks those metrics), and the main concern (framework vs endpoint-faithful + structural tie-break) is already resolvable from the candidate metadata.

The initial pick (PGS004153) is well-justified from the visible records and I do not see a clearly superior direct-match alternative that preserves endpoint fidelity while improving the overall evidence package.

- Endpoint fidelity: PGS004153 is directly aligned to the target (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer). Many other candidates are subtype-specific (ER+/ER−/triple-negative), special populations (e.g., BRCA carriers, male carriers), or different endpoints (e.g., survival/aggressiveness), which are weaker matches for generic “breast carcinoma.”

- Strength among close siblings: Within the same strong, disease-focused evaluation family, PGS004153 has the best reported AUROC (~0.6625) and R² (~0.0764) among the listed siblings (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025/PGS004083 are slightly lower). Those differences are not huge, but they are in the right direction and come without added covariate packaging.

- No need for h2 tool: There is no concrete ambiguity here that heritability would resolve (the chosen model’s reported PRS-centric R² is not obviously implausible on its face, and the main competing “high AUC” models are already explainable by covariate augmentation/framework effects).

PGS000316 remains the best-supported direct-match choice from the visible records. It has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is simply “Coeliac disease”, not a restricted subgroup), and it is evaluated in a very large European validation sample with a strong reported AUROC (0.879, tight CI). The closest apparent competitor on headline AUROC is PGS000040 (AUROC 0.90), but that value is also a full-model metric with unknown covariates and comes from a much smaller validation (n=2,476), making it less robust and not clearly more PRS-comparable than PGS000316. The HLA-DQ2.5-carrier scores (PGS000041/PGS000042) are explicitly subgroup-restricted and therefore less suitable for general celiac disease risk. The UKB framework/portability-family scores either use broader/less specific phenotyping (e.g., “Malabsorption/coeliac disease”) or report non-AUC metrics (partial-r), and—even when they provide PRS-only metrics—come from study archetypes that are typically less reliable than a disease-focused score when a strong direct-endpoint alternative exists. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because the decision hinges on endpoint generality and the relative interpretability/robustness of the reported validation evidence rather than on adjudicating an implausibly high PRS-only R2/AUC claim.

- PGS001299 is the only record with explicit PRS-only discrimination, but it is from the known pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework and its PRS-only AUROC is weak (0.552) with very small PGS-only R² (0.00263); its high full-model AUROC (0.768) is largely covariate-driven (incremental AUROC only 0.00676). This is not a strong basis to displace a disease-focused score.

- PGS003389 shows weak full-model AUROC (0.563) and very low R² (0.00158), so it is not competitive.
- PGS005165 is EAS-only and has modest C-index (0.566); it’s not a better general primary than the EUR-focused disease-meta-analysis LDpred score.

Given the lack of clean PRS-only metrics for most candidates, it is reasonable to prefer the disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis LDpred model with genome-wide coverage (PGS003428) and a moderate HR signal (1.33) over sparse/framework or GWAS-hit-only alternatives whose apparent advantages are mainly full-model discrimination. Heritability lookup is not needed here because no candidate presents a suspiciously high PRS-only R²/AUC that requires an h2 ceiling sanity check.

The key limitation noted by the picker stands: PGS002237’s reported AUROC is a covariate-heavy full-model metric, so it should not be interpreted as PRS-only performance; however, no competing candidate shows cleaner, stronger PRS-only discrimination for an equally direct CKD endpoint, so there is no clear basis to revise. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because the decision is driven by endpoint fidelity and study archetype rather than resolving an AUC-vs-h2 plausibility conflict.

The initial pick (PGS001783) is well-justified from the visible records. It is an exact endpoint match (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and comes from a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; ~884k variants) in a large multi-biobank/global development context, which is generally a stronger evidence pattern than the UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet COPD scores (PGS001332/1333/1334) whose PRS-only AUROCs are low (~0.54) and whose high full-model AUROCs are clearly covariate-driven (tiny incremental AUROC ~0.003). Compared with the UKB portability ‘chronic airway obstruction’ scores (PGS001850/PGS002062), those have only partial-correlation metrics and a less direct endpoint label. Compared with the Commun Biol J44 scores (PGS004466/PGS004536), those report only per-SD ORs with unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable discrimination metric, so they are harder to rank above a candidate with explicit PRS-comparable R2. The main plausible challenger is PGS001788 (same paper/method/endpoint) with much larger validation N, but its reported covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 is materially lower (0.0163 vs 0.0381), so there is no clear reason to revise away from PGS001783.

Confirming PGS004621. PGS000726 is plausible but is a very sparse 12-variant score with limited standalone discrimination reporting (no AUROC/R²; only OR summaries), so it does not clearly surpass PGS004621 on the available metadata. Heritability lookup is not needed here because no candidate provides PRS-only R²/AUC that requires an h2 ceiling sanity check; the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity plus structural/model-quality signals rather than interpreting potentially covariate-inflated PRS-only metrics.

The initial pick (PGS004862) is a clean, endpoint-faithful DCM score with basic covariates and very large EUR validation, so it is a reasonable default. However, the visible candidate set contains a clearly stronger direct-match alternative on PRS-comparable evidence: PGS004951.

No heritability lookup was needed because the decision turns on metric comparability/availability (PRS-only AUC present vs absent), not on whether an unusually high PRS R² exceeds plausible h2 ceilings.

The initial pick (PGS002092) is supported by the visible metadata. Visible candidate evidence supports keeping PGS004944 as the best overall choice for the broad target “glaucoma,” given the available metadata. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable (POAG is a major glaucoma subtype; the record is explicitly POAG, albeit self-reported). Compared with other disease-endpoint candidates, PGS004944 has unusually strong PRS-relevant evidence via effect size (OR=1.74 per SD) and extremely large validation (n=407,667), with a relatively clean/basic covariate set (age/age^2, sex, ancestry) and a reported AUROC (0.748) that, while not PRS-only, is not obviously driven by heavy clinical packaging. The main plausible challenger on “disease-focused + modern genome-wide method + large external validation” is PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto; full-model AUROC 0.777; PRS-only Nagelkerke R2 0.032), but it lacks an effect-size summary here and its AUROC is also full-model; overall it does not clearly dominate PGS004944 on endpoint fidelity, covariate cleanliness, and interpretable PRS contribution taken together. Heritability lookup is not necessary because no candidate presents a suspiciously high PRS-only R2/AUC that needs an h2 ceiling sanity check to adjudicate the pick.

The picker’s choice of PGS004160 is supported by the visible evidence. It is a direct endpoint match (trait_efo=gout; phenotyping_reported=Gout) and sits within a coherent same-endpoint study family (2023 Am J Hum Genet “Evaluation of polygenic scoring methods in five biobanks…”) where covariates are explicitly 0, making the reported AUROC/R2 more comparable across siblings than most other candidates. Within that family, PGS004160 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported discrimination (AUROC ~0.694; R2 ~0.089) relative to close alternatives like LDpred2.CV (PGS004047; AUROC ~0.685; R2 ~0.080) and lassosum.CV (PGS004018; AUROC ~0.678; R2 ~0.073). The main apparent challengers either rely on non-comparable/full-model metrics with heavier or unknown covariates (e.g., PGS000199 AUROC 0.85 in a small clinical setting with unknown covariates), are pan-trait/portability framework outputs with weaker or less interpretable metrics for standalone PRS selection (e.g., PGS001248/001249; PGS002030 partial-r only), or provide effect sizes without a clearer advantage on discrimination/variance explained in a comparable setting (e.g., PGS002762 OR-only). Given the decision hinges on within-family comparability rather than abundant PRS-only metrics across the whole pool, confidence appropriately remains Moderate. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because the selected model’s reported R2 is not an obvious ceiling-violating outlier and there is no concrete ambiguity that h2 would resolve.

Visible evidence supports the picker’s choice. All three candidates are endpoint-aligned to Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (trait_efo matches; phenotyping_reported is the near-synonymous lymphocytic thyroiditis) and are same-family models with the same stated evaluation ancestry set and the same validation N, so phenotype/study context do not separate them. Under the recommended fallback when PRS-only metrics are absent, PGS005271 has the strongest effect-size evidence (OR per SD ≈1.55 vs ≈1.42 and ≈1.04), indicating materially stronger PRS signal, and it uses PRS-CS (genome-wide shrinkage) rather than the much sparser P+T model. Between the two PRS-CS siblings, the OR difference favors PGS005271 despite its slightly lower full-model AUROC than PGS005272, and that is the more defensible tie-break given covariate uncertainty. Heritability lookup is not needed because there is no PRS-comparable R2/AUC to sanity-check against h2.

Visible direct-match candidates split into (a) heart-failure-specific, disease-focused multi-cohort scores with only full-model AUROC reported (e.g., PGS005097 AUROC=0.72 with basic covariates), and (b) other direct-match scores where at least one PRS-comparable metric is explicitly provided. PGS001790 (Heart failure; PRS-CS-auto; eval EUR) reports a PRS-comparable metric: Nagelkerke R² with covariates regressed out (PGS-only R²=0.006981), which is more interpretable for standalone PRS quality than full-model AUROC/C-index values that may be covariate-driven and are not comparable across differing covariate sets. Endpoint fidelity remains exact (heart failure), covariates are standard demographic/PC terms, and validation N is large. Given the picker’s own stated uncertainty that PGS005097’s AUROC is likely full-model and that many alternatives have similar full-model metrics, the presence of an explicit PRS-only metric in PGS001790 is a concrete, record-visible advantage that justifies revising the primary choice.

Confirming PGS002763 as the best available direct-match choice on the visible records. It has the cleanest endpoint alignment to the target (phenotyping_reported = “Hip osteoarthritis”, not a treatment/proxy like total hip replacement or a time-to-event framing), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants) with a reasonable per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) in EUR evaluation—making it the most interpretable standalone PRS signal among candidates that are otherwise missing PRS-only AUC/R².

The main alternative with explicit PRS-only metrics, PGS000967, is from the “813 traits” sparse UKB framework (snpnet; 634 variants) and shows only modest PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.561; R² 0.00628); its much higher full-model AUROC is clearly covariate-driven (incremental AUROC only 0.00918), so it should not displace a disease-focused, endpoint-faithful PRS.

Other candidates are weaker on endpoint fidelity and/or evidence clarity: PGS002728 and PGS002750 are hip replacement/total hip replacement proxies (and PGS002728 reports only a covariate-including full-model AUROC), while PGS004478/PGS004548 have unknown covariates and only modest ORs, and PGS004882 has an implausibly tiny training N (n=404) despite huge evaluation N, making its reported C-index/HR less trustworthy as a PRS-quality signal. Visible candidates include a coherent direct-match Hodgkin’s lymphoma cluster from Cancer PRSweb (PGS000637/638/639/640) with consistent endpoint labeling (“Hodgkin’s disease”), clean/basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and EUR-only evaluation—this is the strongest evidence pattern available for the target trait. Within that sibling set, PGS000639 has the best combined signal (highest reported AUROC among siblings and the strongest per-SD OR), making it a reasonable top pick given the metadata. The only other Hodgkin-labeled option, PGS003449, has clear phenotype-field incoherence (phenotyping_reported indicates chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and a near-null effect size (OR ~1.02), so it should not displace the PRSweb sibling. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity and within-family comparative evidence rather than interpreting an outlier PRS-only R²/AUC against an h2 ceiling (none of these candidates report PRS-only metrics).

PGS004236 is a direct hypertension score with a strong-looking full-model AUROC (0.764) and OR=2.1, but its evaluation is explicitly a covariate-heavy package (sex, age, age^2, study site, race/ethnic background, smoking status, BMI, PCs). With no PRS-only AUROC/R2 reported, that AUROC is not comparable to other candidates and could be substantially covariate-driven. In contrast, PGS001320 is also an exact hypertension endpoint (trait_efo=hypertension; phenotyping_reported=Hypertension) and—critically—reports PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.629; PGS R2 no covariates=0.0649) plus incremental AUROC (0.044) under a basic covariate set (age, sex, array, PCs). That makes its genetic contribution interpretable and directly comparable, avoiding the main limitation flagged in the initial rationale. While PGS001320 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalization risk), within the visible evidence it is the cleanest hypertension candidate on PRS-comparable metrics; other direct-match options either lack PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS004234/PGS004236, PGS004934) or report only partial correlation without AUC/R2 (PGS001838/PGS002047).

Revise away from PGS005265 because its only quantitative support is a full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, making it unclear how much discrimination is attributable to the PRS versus covariate packaging; the per-SD OR is supportive but does not resolve that comparability gap. In contrast, PGS001042 provides explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates = 0.6339; PGS R² no covariates = 0.0236) plus incremental AUROC under basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), which is a cleaner and more directly comparable evidence pattern for standalone PRS performance. Endpoint fidelity remains acceptable for the target (thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism), and between the two snpnet siblings PGS001042 is slightly stronger than PGS001043 on PRS-only R² and AUROC. Although the UKB ‘813 traits’ framework origin is a known generalization risk, in this candidate set it is outweighed by having PRS-only performance reported under clean covariates versus relying on covariate-opaque full-model AUROC.

Visible evidence supports the picker’s choice of PGS004911. Among the four direct-match candidates, PGS004910/PGS004911 are the only ones that look like modern, genome-wide PRS (PRS-CS; ~374k variants) evaluated cleanly with basic demographic/PC covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10) in a large EUR validation (n=343,182). PGS000778 has a much smaller validation sample (n=368) and a more specialized endpoint (clinical events among pathogenic sarcomeric variant carriers), making it less suitable as a general HCM risk PRS. Between the two near-clone 2025 scores, PGS004911 is reasonably preferred: it is the MTAG-labeled sibling from the same study family and shows stronger reported performance/effect sizes (AUROC 0.8; R² 0.048; HR 2.34; OR 1.33 vs lower values for PGS004910) under the same covariate scheme. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity and covariate cleanliness rather than interpreting an implausible PRS-only R² claim.

CONFIRM PGS005218. Among the visible direct-match hypothyroidism candidates, PGS005218 is the only clearly disease-focused, hypothyroidism-specific GWAS/PRS study with very large-scale validation (n=441,692) and a direct endpoint (“Incident hypothyroidism”). The main concern the picker noted is valid: the reported AUROC=0.859 is a full-model metric with near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO) in the covariates, so that AUROC is likely substantially covariate-driven and not a clean PRS-only discrimination estimate; PRS-only AUC/R2 is not provided here. However, the alternatives that do report cleaner PRS-only metrics are predominantly pan-trait/portability framework scores (e.g., PGS000965/PGS001181 from the UKB ‘813 traits’ sparse snpnet paper) or use weaker/shifted endpoints (immune-checkpoint-therapy-induced hypothyroidism: PGS000759/PGS000761/PGS000820), or provide only partial-correlation / incremental-R2 style metrics that are not clearly superior. Therefore keeping PGS005218 as best available is reasonable, with moderated confidence due to biomarker-inflated full-model AUROC and missing PRS-only metrics.

The two available candidates are near-clones on the most important axes: same endpoint labeling (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported “Disorders of iron metabolism” and trait_efo iron metabolism disease), same publication family (UKB portability paper), same training cohort and size, same covariates, and same European validation sample size. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because no candidate reports PRS-only R²/AUC that would benefit from an h2 ceiling sanity check.

Therefore, revise to PGS000053.

Crucially, it reports both PRS-only AUROC=0.63582 and PRS-only R2=0.03413 (plus incremental AUROC), giving a clearer, directly comparable readout of standalone PRS signal than PGS000014’s covariate-adjusted R2 alone.

Given the picker’s own concern that many candidates’ high full-model metrics are covariate-driven and non-comparable, the presence of explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 in PGS001294 is a meaningful upgrade in interpretability for selecting a primary PRS from metadata. I’m not using heritability here because the decision hinges on metric comparability/availability rather than plausibility of an extreme R2.

PGS004253 remains the best-supported direct-match choice on the visible metadata. It has clean endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: ulcerative colitis), a method/architecture that is generally strong for complex traits (LDpred2-auto with genome-wide variant coverage), and—most importantly—reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.84, 95% CI 1.76–1.93), which is a robust PRS-quality signal even when PRS-only AUROC/R² are not explicitly provided. The competing candidates are largely from pan-trait or portability framework papers: PGS001306/PGS001307 (snpnet sparse ‘813 traits’ UKB framework) and PGS001855/PGS002066 (‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores’), which either provide weaker/less comparable performance evidence (partial-r only; AUROC=0.57 with unknown covariates; missing PRS-only metrics) and/or carry the known framework generalization penalty. PGS001307 also adds a time-to-event endpoint mismatch for a generic UC risk target. While PGS004253’s AUROC appears to be full-model (so not perfectly comparable to PRS-only AUROC), its covariates are basic and the strong OR evidence plus endpoint/method coherence still outweigh the alternatives. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because the decision does not hinge on adjudicating an implausibly high PRS-only R²/AUC claim.

Visible records support the picker’s choice. Most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R², so the very high full-model AUROC values in PGS000071/PGS000782 (~0.80) are not comparable as standalone PRS performance and are plausibly driven by their extensive covariate set (age/sex/PCs plus smoking variables and BMI). In contrast, the Cancer PRSweb cluster (PGS000607–PGS000616) is internally comparable: same endpoint family (“Cancer of bladder”), basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch), and similar evaluation setting. Within that cluster, PGS000611 (GWAS hits, 13 variants; UKB dev; EUR eval) has one of the strongest and cleanest risk-stratification signals reported (OR top 1% vs rest = 2.66, CI 1.79–3.93) while maintaining similar per-SD OR (~1.28) and AUROC (~0.57) to close siblings, making it a reasonable primary among the most comparable set. Alternatives either (a) have weaker/less interpretable metrics (e.g., partial-r only in portability scores), (b) have unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS000152), or (c) shift phenotype (urothelial carcinoma) and still lack comparable discrimination metrics (PGS003335). No heritability lookup is needed because the main uncertainty is metric comparability/covariate packaging rather than plausibility of a PRS-only R² claim.

Confirming PGS002075 as the best available choice from the visible candidates. It has the cleanest endpoint alignment to the target trait (urolithiasis via “Urinary calculus”, trait_efo=urolithiasis) and, among the two portability-paper siblings with comparable phenotype/covariates/validation context (PGS001864 vs PGS002075), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with much broader variant coverage and a slightly stronger PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0385 vs 0.0323 in EUR). The main alternative with explicit AUROC (PGS001250) is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework and its headline AUROC is largely full-model/covariate-driven (PGS-only AUROC ~0.567; small incremental AUROC), making it less compelling as a standalone PRS despite having more complete metrics. The 2024 Commun Biol models (PGS004493/PGS004563) are endpoint-close but provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.23–1.28) with unknown covariates and no discrimination metrics, so they do not clearly surpass the LDpred2 portability score on the available evidence. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity and the relative quality/interpretability of the reported PRS-comparable metrics rather than on adjudicating an implausibly high PRS R²/AUC.

Visible candidates include both exact/umbrella uterine cancer endpoints (e.g., PGS000541/PGS000542/PGS001795) and endometrial-carcinoma endpoints (dominant uterine subtype) including PGS003381. On the metadata shown, PGS003381 has the strongest overall evidence package for the target concept: high endpoint fidelity to a uterine cancer diagnosis subtype (phenotyping_reported: uterine endometrial carcinoma), a genome-wide construction with substantial variant coverage (lassosum; 529,365 variants), and evaluation with relatively clean/basic covariates (age + genetic PCs). The main alternatives either (a) are small GWAS-hits/P+T uterine scores with clearly weaker discrimination (PGS000541/PGS000542 full-model AUROC ~0.57), or (b) are framework-style global-biobank PRS (PGS001795) that does provide a PRS-comparable R2 but it is very small and the study archetype is less disease-focused, making it a weaker replacement despite the metric type advantage. Several endometrial scores report higher full-model AUROC (~0.75) but are based on very small SNP sets and/or include heavier covariate packaging (e.g., family history, BMI, reproductive factors), so their AUROC is less attributable to the PRS itself than PGS003381’s cleaner setup. Heritability lookup is not needed here because the decision is driven by endpoint fidelity + method/variant coverage + covariate cleanliness, and no candidate presents a PRS-only R2/AUC close to a plausible h2 ceiling that would create a concrete sanity-check conflict.

PGS000738 remains the best choice among the three visible candidates because it is the only one whose publication context and stated trait align with generic vitiligo risk in a disease-focused way. The two alternatives have clearer, more consequential issues: (1) PGS000760 is labeled “Vitiligo” but its phenotyping_reported is explicitly about anti–PD-L1–induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients, making it endpoint-mismatched for vitiligo prediction despite having an HR; (2) PGS001536 has cleaner PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC/R²) but is from the “813 traits in UK Biobank” sparse framework family and uses a time-to-event vitiligo endpoint, which is a weaker archetype when a disease-focused direct model exists. PGS000738’s own metadata is imperfect (phenotyping_reported shows ‘Red hair’ and it reports pseudo-R² rather than PRS-only AUROC), but those issues are less damaging than the explicit endpoint mismatch in PGS000760 and the framework/TTE penalties for PGS001536. Heritability lookup is not necessary here because the decision turns on endpoint fidelity and study archetype rather than interpreting an unusually high PRS-only R²/AUC.
